blocks.text: `docker history` maps size to instructions, `docker image inspect` shows the runtime config, and `dive` exposes wasted space inside layers.

$ docker history --no-trunc --format '{{.Size}}\t{{.CreatedBy}}' rag-api:dev
2.31GB  RUN pip install -r requirements.txt     # usually CUDA torch on a CPU service
$ docker image inspect rag-api:dev --format '{{json .Config}}' | jq '{User,Entrypoint,Cmd,Env,ExposedPorts}'
$ dive rag-api:dev

rows: Which instruction added how many bytes
User, Entrypoint/Cmd, Env, WorkingDir, Volumes, Architecture
Per-layer file tree, files added then deleted, efficiency score (CI gate possible)

blocks.text: What to check on an unfamiliar image

items: Runs as root or a non-root UID?

blocks.text: History and config are public to anyone who pulls: every ENV value and any build ARG used in RUN is visible. Use BuildKit secret mounts for build-time secrets.

Q: "An image is 4 GB. How do you find out why?" A: "Sort docker history by size to find the heavy instruction, then open those layers in dive to spot caches, test data, .git, duplicated dependencies or CUDA wheels, and fix the Dockerfile at that step."

items: history → where the bytes come from.
inspect → what will actually run and as whom.
Image metadata is public; never put secrets there.
